- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R49): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.48-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and was 1.52, 1.52, 1.51, 1.50, 1.49, 1.50, 1.50, 1.49 at R42-R49. c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.49-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.
- Myopic optimum is p = (A/100 + 1)/2 with A = 77.4 + 80c (minus the low-c correction). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). At c=1.55 it is about 1.51 (about $25.6). At c=1.60 it is about 1.53 (about $27.8). At c=1.62 it is about 1.535 (about $28.7). At c=1.75 it is about 1.58 (about $34). The profit curve is very flat: 1 cent off the optimum costs about $0.01, and 5 cents off costs about $0.30. 1.48 (R25) cost about $0.12 vs 1.52. At c=1.52, 1.49 (R29) and 1.50 (R31/R33/R43) both gave $24.29.
- Pricing well above c is costly (R15 and R16 at p−c = 0.30 and 0.35 gave $18 and $16).
- Follower hypothesis is rejected. c_t = p_{t-1} held in R14, R18 and R19 but failed in R13, R15-R17 and R20-R49. Raising our price didn't lift c. Treat c as exogenous and noisy.
- Matched-price demand (c = p) is concave. Its profit optimum is about $1.95-$2.00 at about $34.
- Robust range: $1.49-$1.65 when c is low. Avoid prices above $2.40, well below $1.48, and above 1.85 when c is about 1.6.

Observations:
- Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/R76/R78/R80, R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/R75/R77/R79/R81, R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).
- Global linear fit: q ≈ 37.45 − 93(p − 1.9) + 58(c − 1.9). It is good within about 2 units, but demand is convex at high p−c (R16 is underpredicted).
- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R81): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.47-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and has been in 1.47-1.52 at R42-R81 (mostly 1.49/1.50, recently alternating, with occasional 1.52 blips at R60, R63, R70). c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.47-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.
- Myopic optimum is p = (A/100 + 1)/2 with A = 77.4 + 80c (minus the low-c correction). At c=1.47 it is about 1.475 (about $22.3). At c=1.49 it is about 1.48 (about $23.0; 1.48 and 1.49 differ by about $0.01). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7 by formula, but $23.44 realized). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). At c=1.55 it is about 1.51 (about $25.6). At c=1.60 it is about 1.53 (about $27.8). At c=1.62 it is about 1.535 (about $28.7). At c=1.75 it is about 1.58 (about $34). The profit curve is very flat: 1 cent off the optimum costs about $0.01, and 5 cents off costs about $0.30. 1.48 (R25) cost about $0.12 vs 1.52. At c=1.52, 1.48 (R60/R70), 1.49 (R29/R63) and 1.50 (R31/R33/R43) all gave about $24.28-24.29. At c=1.50, 1.48 and 1.49 both give $23.44.
- Pricing well above c is costly (R15 and R16 at p−c = 0.30 and 0.35 gave $18 and $16).
- Follower hypothesis is rejected. c_t = p_{t-1} held in R14, R18 and R19 but failed in R13, R15-R17 and R20-R81. Raising our price didn't lift c. Treat c as exogenous and noisy.
- Matched-price demand (c = p) is concave. Its profit optimum is about $1.95-$2.00 at about $34.
- Robust range: $1.48-$1.65 when c is low. Avoid prices above $2.40, well below $1.45, and above 1.85 when c is about 1.6.

Observations:
- Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/R76/R78/R80/R82/R84/R86/R88, R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/R75/R77/R79/R81/R83/R85/R87/R89, R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).
- Global linear fit: q ≈ 37.45 − 93(p − 1.9) + 58(c − 1.9). It is good within about 2 units, but demand is convex at high p−c (R16 is underpredicted).
- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R89): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.47-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and has been in 1.47-1.52 at R42-R89 (mostly 1.49/1.50, recently alternating, with occasional 1.52 blips at R60, R63, R70). c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.47-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.
- Myopic optimum is p = (A/100 + 1)/2 with A = 77.4 + 80c (minus the low-c correction). At c=1.47 it is about 1.475 (about $22.3). At c=1.49 it is about 1.48 (about $23.0; 1.48 and 1.49 differ by about $0.01). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7 by formula, but $23.44 realized). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). At c=1.52, 1.48 (R60/R70), 1.49 (R29/R63) and 1.50 (R31/R33/R43) all gave about $24.28-24.29. At c=1.50, 1.48 and 1.49 both give $23.44.

- Follower hypothesis is rejected. c_t = p_{t-1} held in R14, R18 and R19 but failed in R13, R15-R17 and R20-R89. Raising our price didn't lift c. Treat c as exogenous and noisy.
- Matched-price demand (c = p) is concave. Its profit optimum is about $1.95-$2.00 at about $34.

Observations:
- Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R96 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R95 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).
- Global linear fit: q ≈ 37.45 − 93(p − 1.9) + 58(c − 1.9). It is good within about 2 units, but demand is convex at high p−c (R16 is underpredicted).
- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R96): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.47-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and has been in 1.47-1.52 at R42-R96 (mostly 1.49/1.50, recently strictly alternating, with occasional 1.52 blips at R60, R63, R70). c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.47-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.
- Myopic optimum is p = (A/100 + 1)/2 with A = 77.4 + 80c (minus the low-c correction). At c=1.47 it is about 1.475 (about $22.3). At c=1.49 it is about 1.48 (about $23.0; 1.48 and 1.49 differ by about $0.01). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7 by formula, but $23.44 realized). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). The profit curve is very flat: 1 cent off the optimum costs about $0.01, and 5 cents off costs about $0.30. 1.48 (R25) cost about $0.12 vs 1.52. - Follower hypothesis is rejected. c_t = p_{t-1} held in R14, R18 and R19 but failed in R13, R15-R17 and R20-R96. Raising our price didn't lift c. Treat c as exogenous and noisy.
- Matched-price demand (c = p) is concave. Its profit optimum is about $1.95-$2.00 at about $34.

Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R104 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R103 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).

- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R104): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).

Observations:
- Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R110 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R111 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).
- Global linear fit: q ≈ 37.45 − 93(p − 1.9) + 58(c − 1.9). It is good within about 2 units, but demand is convex at high p−c (R16 is underpredicted).
- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R111): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.47-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and has been in 1.47-1.52 at R42-R111 (mostly 1.49/1.50, strictly alternating since R71, with occasional 1.52 blips at R60, R63, R70). c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.47-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.
- Myopic optimum is p = (A/100 + 1)/2 with A = 77.4 + 80c (minus the low-c correction). At c=1.47 it is about 1.475 (about $22.3). At c=1.49 it is about 1.48 (about $23.0; 1.48 and 1.49 differ by about $0.01). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7 by formula, but $23.44 realized). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). At c=1.55 it is about 1.51 (about $25.6). At c=1.60 it is about 1.53 (about $27.8). At c=1.62 it is about 1.535 (about $28.7). At c=1.75 it is about 1.58 (about $34). The profit curve is very flat: 1 cent off the optimum costs about $0.01, and 5 cents off costs about $0.30. 1.48 (R25) cost about $0.12 vs 1.52. At c=1.52, 1.48 (R60/R70), 1.49 (R29/R63) and 1.50 (R31/R33/R43) all gave about $24.28-24.29. At c=1.50, 1.48 and 1.49 both give $23.44.
- Pricing well above c is costly (R15 and R16 at p−c = 0.30 and 0.35 gave $18 and $16).
- Follower hypothesis is rejected. c_t = p_{t-1} held in R14, R18 and R19 but failed in R13, R15-R17 and R20-R111. Raising our price didn't lift c (even over 2 consecutive rounds at R15-R16). Treat c as exogenous and noisy.
- Matched-price demand (c = p) is concave. Its profit optimum is about $1.95-$2.00 at about $34.
- Robust range: $1.48-$1.65 when c is low. Avoid prices above $2.40, well below $1.45, and above 1.85 when c is about 1.6.

- Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). - Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R115): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). Observations:
- Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R118 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R117 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).
- Global linear fit: q ≈ 37.45 − 93(p − 1.9) + 58(c − 1.9). It is good within about 2 units, but demand is convex at high p−c (R16 is underpredicted).
- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R118): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.47-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and has been in 1.47-1.52 at R42-R118 (mostly 1.49/1.50, strictly alternating since R71, with occasional 1.52 blips at R60, R63, R70). c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.47-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.
- Myopic optimum is p = (A/100 + 1)/2 with A = 77.4 + 80c (minus the low-c correction). At c=1.47 it is about 1.475 (about $22.3). At c=1.49 it is about 1.48 (about $23.0; 1.48 and 1.49 differ by about $0.01). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7 by formula, but $23.44 realized). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). At c=1.55 it is about 1.51 (about $25.6). At c=1.60 it is about 1.53 (about $27.8). At c=1.62 it is about 1.535 (about $28.7). At c=1.75 it is about 1.58 (about $34). The profit curve is very flat: 1 cent off the optimum costs about $0.01, and 5 cents off costs about $0.30. 1.48 (R25) cost about $0.12 vs 1.52. At c=1.52, 1.48 (R60/R70), 1.49 (R29/R63) and 1.50 (R31/R33/R43) all gave about $24.28-24.29. At c=1.50, 1.48 and 1.49 both give $23.44.

- Follower hypothesis is rejected. c_t = p_{t-1} held in R14, R18 and R19 but failed in R13, R15-R17 and R20-R118. Raising our price didn't lift c (even over 2 consecutive rounds at R15-R16). Treat c as exogenous and noisy.
- Matched-price demand (c = p) is concave. Its profit optimum is about $1.95-$2.00 at about $34, but c is exogenous so this is not reachable.
- Robust range: $1.48-$1.65 when c is low. Avoid prices above $2.40, well below $1.45, and above 1.85 when c is about 1.6.

Observations:
- Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R126 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R125 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).
- Global linear fit: q ≈ 37.45 − 93(p − 1.9) + 58(c − 1.9). It is good within about 2 units, but demand is convex at high p−c (R16 is underpredicted).
- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R126): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.47-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and has been in 1.47-1.52 at R42-R126 (mostly 1.49/1.50, strictly alternating since R71, with occasional 1.52 blips at R60, R63, R70). c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.47-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.
- Myopic optimum is p = (A/100 + 1)/2 with A = 77.4 + 80c (minus the low-c correction). At c=1.47 it is about 1.475 (about $22.3). At c=1.49 it is about 1.48 (about $23.0; 1.48 and 1.49 differ by about $0.01). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7 by formula, but $23.44 realized). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). At c=1.55 it is about 1.51 (about $25.6). At c=1.60 it is about 1.53 (about $27.8). At c=1.62 it is about 1.535 (about $28.7). At c=1.75 it is about 1.58 (about $34). The profit curve is very flat: 1 cent off the optimum costs about $0.01, and 5 cents off costs about $0.30. 1.48 (R25) cost about $0.12 vs 1.52. At c=1.52, 1.48 (R60/R70), 1.49 (R29/R63) and 1.50 (R31/R33/R43) all gave about $24.28-24.29. At c=1.50, 1.48 and 1.49 both give $23.44.
- Pricing well above c is costly (R15 and R16 at p−c = 0.30 and 0.35 gave $18 and $16).
- Follower hypothesis is rejected. c_t = p_{t-1} held in R14, R18 and R19 but failed in R13, R15-R17 and R20-R126. Raising our price didn't lift c (even over 2 consecutive rounds at R15-R16). Treat c as exogenous and noisy.
- Matched-price demand (c = p) is concave. Its profit optimum is about $1.95-$2.00 at about $34, but c is exogenous so this is not reachable.
- Robust range: $1.48-$1.65 when c is low. Avoid prices above $2.40, well below $1.45, and above 1.85 when c is about 1.6.

Observations:
- Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R134 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R133 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).
- Global linear fit: q ≈ 37.45 − 93(p − 1.9) + 58(c − 1.9). It is good within about 2 units, but demand is convex at high p−c (R16 is underpredicted).
- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R134): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.47-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and has been in 1.47-1.52 at R42-R134 (mostly 1.49/1.50, strictly alternating since R71, with occasional 1.52 blips at R60, R63, R70). c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.47-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.
- Myopic optimum is p = (A/100 + 1)/2 with A = 77.4 + 80c (minus the low-c correction). At c=1.47 it is about 1.475 (about $22.3). At c=1.49 it is about 1.48 (about $23.0; 1.48 and 1.49 differ by about $0.01). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7 by formula, but $23.44 realized). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). At c=1.55 it is about 1.51 (about $25.6). At c=1.60 it is about 1.53 (about $27.8). At c=1.62 it is about 1.535 (about $28.7). At c=1.75 it is about 1.58 (about $34). The profit curve is very flat: 1 cent off the optimum costs about $0.01, and 5 cents off costs about $0.30. 1.48 (R25) cost about $0.12 vs 1.52. At c=1.52, 1.48 (R60/R70), 1.49 (R29/R63) and 1.50 (R31/R33/R43) all gave about $24.28-24.29. At c=1.50, 1.48 and 1.49 both give $23.44.
- Pricing well above c is costly (R15 and R16 at p−c = 0.30 and 0.35 gave $18 and $16).
- Follower hypothesis is rejected. c_t = p_{t-1} held in R14, R18 and R19 but failed in R13, R15-R17 and R20-R134. Raising our price didn't lift c (even over 2 consecutive rounds at R15-R16). Treat c as exogenous and noisy.
- Matched-price demand (c = p) is concave. Its profit optimum is about $1.95-$2.00 at about $34, but c is exogenous so this is not reachable.
- Robust range: $1.48-$1.65 when c is low. Avoid prices above $2.40, well below $1.45, and above 1.85 when c is about 1.6.

Observations:
- Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R142 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R141 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).
- Global linear fit: q ≈ 37.45 − 93(p − 1.9) + 58(c − 1.9). It is good within about 2 units, but demand is convex at high p−c (R16 is underpredicted).
- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R142): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.47-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and has been in 1.47-1.52 at R42-R142 (mostly 1.49/1.50, strictly alternating since R71, with occasional 1.52 blips at R60, R63, R70). c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.47-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.
- Myopic optimum is p = (A/100 + 1)/2 with A = 77.4 + 80c (minus the low-c correction). At c=1.47 it is about 1.475 (about $22.3). At c=1.49 it is about 1.48 (about $23.0; 1.48 and 1.49 differ by about $0.01). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7 by formula, but $23.44 realized). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). - Follower hypothesis is rejected. c_t = p_{t-1} held in R14, R18 and R19 but failed in R13, R15-R17 and R20-R142. Raising our price didn't lift c (even over 2 consecutive rounds at R15-R16). Treat c as exogenous and noisy.
- Matched-price demand (c = p) is concave. Its profit optimum is about $1.95-$2.00 at about $34, but c is exogenous so this is not reachable.

Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R150 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R149 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).

- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R150): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).

Don't extrapolate from a single value.

- Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R158 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R157 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).
- Global linear fit: q ≈ 37.45 − 93(p − 1.9) + 58(c − 1.9). It is good within about 2 units, but demand is convex at high p−c (R16 is underpredicted).
- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R158): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.47-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and has been in 1.47-1.52 at R42-R158 (mostly 1.49/1.50, strictly alternating since R71, with occasional 1.52 blips at R60, R63, R70). c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.47-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.
- Myopic optimum is p = (A/100 + 1)/2 with A = 77.4 + 80c (minus the low-c correction). At c=1.47 it is about 1.475 (about $22.3). At c=1.49 it is about 1.48 (about $23.0; 1.48 and 1.49 differ by about $0.01). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7 by formula, but $23.44 realized). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R160 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R159 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).

- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R160): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). Observations:
- Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R166 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R165 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).
- Global linear fit: q ≈ 37.45 − 93(p − 1.9) + 58(c − 1.9). It is good within about 2 units, but demand is convex at high p−c (R16 is underpredicted).
- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R166): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.47-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and has been in 1.47-1.52 at R42-R166 (mostly 1.49/1.50, strictly alternating since R71, with occasional 1.52 blips at R60, R63, R70). c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.47-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.
- Myopic optimum is p = (A/100 + 1)/2 with A = 77.4 + 80c (minus the low-c correction). At c=1.47 it is about 1.475 (about $22.3). At c=1.49 it is about 1.48 (about $23.0; 1.48 and 1.49 differ by about $0.01). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7 by formula, but $23.44 realized). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). - Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R172 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R173 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).
- Global linear fit: q ≈ 37.45 − 93(p − 1.9) + 58(c − 1.9). It is good within about 2 units, but demand is convex at high p−c (R16 is underpredicted).
- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R173): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.47-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and has been in 1.47-1.52 at R42-R173 (mostly 1.49/1.50, strictly alternating since R71, with occasional 1.52 blips at R60, R63, R70). c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.47-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.

At c=1.49 it is about 1.48 (about $23.0; 1.48 and 1.49 differ by about $0.01). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7 by formula, but $23.44 realized). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). - Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R174 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R173 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).
- Global linear fit: q ≈ 37.45 − 93(p − 1.9) + 58(c − 1.9). It is good within about 2 units, but demand is convex at high p−c (R16 is underpredicted).
- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R174): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.47-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and has been in 1.47-1.52 at R42-R174 (mostly 1.49/1.50, strictly alternating since R71, with occasional 1.52 blips at R60, R63, R70). c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.47-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.
- Myopic optimum is p = (A/100 + 1)/2 with A = 77.4 + 80c (minus the low-c correction). At c=1.47 it is about 1.475 (about $22.3). At c=1.49 it is about 1.48 (about $23.0; 1.48 and 1.49 differ by about $0.01). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7 by formula, but $23.44 realized). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). - Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R182 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R181 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).
- Global linear fit: q ≈ 37.45 − 93(p − 1.9) + 58(c − 1.9). It is good within about 2 units, but demand is convex at high p−c (R16 is underpredicted).
- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R182): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.47-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and has been in 1.47-1.52 at R42-R182 (mostly 1.49/1.50, strictly alternating since R71, with occasional 1.52 blips at R60, R63, R70). c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.47-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.
- Myopic optimum is p = (A/100 + 1)/2 with A = 77.4 + 80c (minus the low-c correction). At c=1.47 it is about 1.475 (about $22.3). At c=1.49 it is about 1.48 (about $23.0; 1.48 and 1.49 differ by about $0.01). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7 by formula, but $23.44 realized). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). Observations:
- Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R190 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R191 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).
- Global linear fit: q ≈ 37.45 − 93(p − 1.9) + 58(c − 1.9). It is good within about 2 units, but demand is convex at high p−c (R16 is underpredicted).
- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R191): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.47-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and has been in 1.47-1.52 at R42-R191 (mostly 1.49/1.50, strictly alternating since R71, with occasional 1.52 blips at R60, R63, R70). c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.47-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.
- Myopic optimum is p = (A/100 + 1)/2 with A = 77.4 + 80c (minus the low-c correction). At c=1.47 it is about 1.475 (about $22.3). At c=1.49 it is about 1.48 (about $23.0; 1.48 and 1.49 differ by about $0.01). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7 by formula, but $23.44 realized). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). At c=1.55 it is about 1.51 (about $25.6). At c=1.60 it is about 1.53 (about $27.8). At c=1.62 it is about 1.535 (about $28.7). At c=1.75 it is about 1.58 (about $34). The profit curve is very flat: 1 cent off the optimum costs about $0.01, and 5 cents off costs about $0.30. 1.48 (R25) cost about $0.12 vs 1.52. At c=1.52, 1.48 (R60/R70), 1.49 (R29/R63) and 1.50 (R31/R33/R43) all gave about $24.28-24.29. At c=1.50, 1.48 and 1.49 both give $23.44.
- Pricing well above c is costly (R15 and R16 at p−c = 0.30 and 0.35 gave $18 and $16).
- Follower hypothesis is rejected. c_t = p_{t-1} held in R14, R18 and R19 but failed in R13, R15-R17 and R20-R191. Raising our price didn't lift c (even over 2 consecutive rounds at R15-R16). Treat c as exogenous and noisy.
- Matched-price demand (c = p) is concave. Its profit optimum is about $1.95-$2.00 at about $34, but c is exogenous so this is not reachable.
- Robust range: $1.48-$1.65 when c is low. Avoid prices above $2.40, well below $1.45, and above 1.85 when c is about 1.6.

Observations:
- Demand depends on our price and the competitor's price, with no noise given (p, c). Repeats are confirmed many times (R3/R12, R18/R20, R29/R63, R31/R33/R43, R37/R38/R46/R49/R51/R53/R65-R68/R72/R74/.../R198 (even rounds), R34/R44, R28/R45, R47/R48/R50/R52/R61/R62/R64/R71/R73/.../R199 (odd rounds), R56/R57/R59, R58/R69, R60/R70).
- Global linear fit: q ≈ 37.45 − 93(p − 1.9) + 58(c − 1.9). It is good within about 2 units, but demand is convex at high p−c (R16 is underpredicted).
- Local fit (confirmed by R19 and R21-R199): q ≈ 77.4 − 100p + 80c, i.e. 50.4 − 100(p−1.55) + 80(c−1.60). It overpredicts by about 0.3-0.7 when c ≤ 1.53, so use about 0.45 lower A there (about 0.65-0.7 at c≈1.47-1.50). It also overpredicts by about 1 at c = 1.75 (R39), so the c-slope may be slightly below 80 at higher c. The correction fades out around c≈1.535-1.54 (R41 at c=1.58 needed none).
- Profit is driven mostly by c, which we can't control. c drifted down from about 2.0 (R6) to 1.50 (R28), stayed in 1.48-1.54 (R26-R38), spiked to 1.75 at R39, returned to 1.49 at R40, was 1.58 at R41, and has been in 1.47-1.52 at R42-R199 (mostly 1.49/1.50, strictly alternating since R71, with occasional 1.52 blips at R60, R63, R70). c is volatile with one-round spikes of about 0.1-0.25, but it mean-reverts to about 1.47-1.55. Don't extrapolate from a single value.
- Myopic optimum is p = (A/100 + 1)/2 with A = 77.4 + 80c (minus the low-c correction). At c=1.47 it is about 1.475 (about $22.3). At c=1.49 it is about 1.48 (about $23.0; 1.48 and 1.49 differ by about $0.01). At c=1.50 it is about 1.485 (about $23.7 by formula, but $23.44 realized). At c=1.52 it is about 1.493 (about $24.2). At c=1.55 it is about 1.51 (about $25.6). At c=1.60 it is about 1.53 (about $27.8). At c=1.62 it is about 1.535 (about $28.7). At c=1.75 it is about 1.58 (about $34). The profit curve is very flat: 1 cent off the optimum costs about $0.01, and 5 cents off costs about $0.30. 1.48 (R25) cost about $0.12 vs 1.52. At c=1.52, 1.48 (R60/R70), 1.49 (R29/R63) and 1.50 (R31/R33/R43) all gave about $24.28-24.29. At c=1.50, 1.48 and 1.49 both give $23.44.
- Pricing well above c is costly (R15 and R16 at p−c = 0.30 and 0.35 gave $18 and $16).
- Follower hypothesis is rejected. c_t = p_{t-1} held in R14, R18 and R19 but failed in R13, R15-R17 and R20-R199. Raising our price didn't lift c (even over 2 consecutive rounds at R15-R16). Treat c as exogenous and noisy.
- Matched-price demand (c = p) is concave. Its profit optimum is about $1.95-$2.00 at about $34, but c is exogenous so this is not reachable.
- Robust range: $1.48-$1.65 when c is low. Avoid prices above $2.40, well below $1.45, and above 1.85 when c is about 1.6.
